slip.document:
# Tidewater Queue Service Maintenance Change Record
Change CHG-2641 | 06/18/2026 | Owner: Ethan Weaver

## Scope
Tidewater Harbor Systems will fix a retry bug that caused duplicate notifications when the worker restarted during a network timeout. Dmitri Abbott reviewed the patch; Colleen Navarro is the release operator. The change updates the worker image from 4.18.2 to 4.18.3 and adds a database migration for the notification status field. The migration is backward-incompatible: the prior worker cannot read the new status value after it is written.

## Deployment plan
- Confirm the 4.18.3 image passes CI and the staging replay test for 500 queued notifications.
- Apply migration 2026_06_18_add_status, then deploy image 4.18.3 to one canary instance.
- Check queue depth, duplicate-notification count, and worker error rate for 15 minutes before completing the fleet rollout.
- Notify support after production verification; record the deployment timestamp in CHG-2641.

The production health check runs every 30 seconds. The deployment configuration specifies the following interval:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| health_check_interval_seconds | 15 |
| canary_instances | 1 |
| rollout_batch_size | 2 |

## Rollback and verification
- Rollback: redeploy image tag 4.18.2.
- Stop rollout if the error rate exceeds 1% or queue depth rises above 2,000 messages.
- After rollout, verify that a retried notification is delivered once and that no worker errors appear in the logs.

Ethan will attach the CI run and staging replay results to the change record before the scheduled 10:00 AM deployment window. Production monitoring remains assigned to Colleen through 10:30 AM.

errors.quote: The production health check runs every 30 seconds.
errors.explanation: The deployment configuration table specifies health_check_interval_seconds as 15, contradicting the stated 30-second interval.
errors.fix: The production health check runs every 15 seconds.

errors.explanation: The migration is explicitly backward-incompatible, so redeploying the old worker alone will not restore service compatibility after the new status value is written. The rollback instructions omit a database migration rollback or other recovery step.
errors.fix: Rollback: stop writes, restore the database to its pre-migration state, then redeploy image tag 4.18.2.
